title: How an Ice Maker Works in 60 Seconds 🧊❄️ #shorts
description:
A fridge ice maker makes ice all by itself. A valve fills a tray with water, a thermostat waits until it freezes, a tiny heater loosens the cubes, and a rotating arm pushes them into the bin. A wire arm stops the cycle when the bin is full. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#icemaker #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Your fridge makes ice *all by itself*, batch after batch, and you never touch a tray.

steps.label: Fill
steps.text: First, an electric *water valve* opens for a few seconds and fills a curved metal tray.

steps.label: Freeze
steps.text: Freezing air chills the tray, while a *thermostat* waits until the water is solid ice.

steps.label: Loosen
steps.text: Then a small *heater* under the tray warms it just enough to free the cubes.

steps.label: Eject
steps.text: A little motor turns *ejector arms* that lift the cubes out and sweep them into the bin.

steps.label: Full
steps.text: A *wire arm* rests on top of the ice. When the bin is full, it lifts and stops the cycle.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Fill, freeze, *eject*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
